## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Hatthanillehaka Sikkhāpada* ("Licking the hand") is the fifty-second training rule of the *Sekhiya* chapter in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like other training rules in this section, it establishes proper etiquette regarding eating and decorum for Buddhist monastics, prohibiting the licking of one's hands while taking food [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, an English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
This training rule is attested across nearly all major early Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, and the *Parivāra*, as well as Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya traditions including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya texts [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies 103 matching passages shared with 46 other Pali texts, reflecting the repetitive formulaic structure of the *Sekhiya* training rules; the closest internal reuse occurs with adjacent and thematic rules such as *Sekhiya* 54, 68, 53, and 15 [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
